hints: Focus on the oxidation ladder, only primary alcohols and aldehydes can climb all the way up to a carboxylic acid.
Check the first two compounds, propanal is an aldehyde so it oxidises easily, but propanone is a ketone which resists this oxidant.
Compare the two alcohols, the primary alcohol can go through aldehyde to acid under reflux, while the secondary alcohol stops at a ketone.
walkthrough:
**Recall what hot acidified dichromate does**

This is a strong oxidising agent. Under reflux with excess, oxidation goes as far as possible.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$ $$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone (stops here)}$$ $$\text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$ Ketones are not oxidised (except C-C cleavage, not at A Level).

**Test each compound in turn**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is propanal, an aldehyde. It gains one O to give propanoic acid. Yes.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ is propanone, a ketone. No reaction. No.

**Test the two alcohols and count**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is propan-1-ol, a primary alcohol. With excess and reflux it goes fully to propanoic acid. Yes.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. It oxidises only to propanone, not to an acid. No.

That is 1 + 1 = 2 compounds that give a carboxylic acid.

options.A: 1 is too low. You get this if you count only one of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Remember both an aldehyde and a primary alcohol give the acid under reflux with excess oxidant.
options.B: 2 is correct. Only propanal and propan-1-ol produce a carboxylic acid. Propanone is unreactive and propan-2-ol stops at a ketone.
options.C: 3 is incorrect. This usually comes from wrongly including the secondary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones, and ketones do not oxidise further to acids with $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$.
options.D: 4 is incorrect. This assumes all carbonyl compounds and alcohols give acids. Ketones like $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ are resistant to oxidation, and secondary alcohols stop at the ketone stage.
